A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ImageRAG by the same authors. Their text, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation benchmarks, ablations, proprietary-retrieval experiments and a user study with 46 participants and 767 comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds FLUX-based results, additional datasets, VLM diagnostic tests and expanded human evaluations.

M1.justification: The core VLM diagnosis, caption generation, retrieval and reference-conditioning workflow remains unchanged, including the prompts and error fallback. v2 Section 3.2 adds optional similarity-threshold filtering and repeated generation until VLM-confirmed alignment. These are proposed procedural options; Appendix A explicitly states that experiments use no retrieval threshold.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix E.1 adds fine-grained generation using Stanford Dogs, Oxford Flowers and Stanford Cars, including their images in retrieval. It also adds a VLM concept-identification task and explicit mismatched-retrieval scenarios. ImageNet, iNaturalist, CUB, Aircraft and personalization remain covered; Aircraft results survive in Appendix E.

E2.justification: FLUX joins the comparative human study in v2 Figure 4, having previously appeared only in automatic comparisons. The new diagnostic experiment compares GPT-4o with Gemini, Qwen2.5-VL-7B and LLaVA. Most generation comparators remain, but Aircraft loses its original full baseline comparison, including Pixart-Σ and GraPE-O.

E3.justification: v2 adds GPTScore, CLIP-I evaluation on additional datasets, and evaluation of ImageRAG with FLUX/OminiControl. Human evaluation expands from 46 participants and 767 comparisons to 67 participants, 977 comparisons and 231 absolute judgments. The absolute study selects cases where the VLM triggered retrieval. Appendix E.5 introduces a controlled diagnostic protocol with 20 classes and 780 prompts.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled tests of VLM concept recognition, seed-based diversity comparisons, concrete retrieval/counting/text failure cases, and qualitative component-ablation examples. The original prompt-rephrasing, retrieval-caption, retriever-choice and retrieval-dataset-size ablations are retained, sometimes relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix E.6 newly reports generation with different seeds, showing five outputs per prompt in Figures 17–19. It does not provide seed identities or aggregate repeated-run uncertainty. Existing mean-plus-standard-error tables and comparative-study error bars remain; no new significance-testing procedure is specified.

E6.justification: Most retained OmniGen/SDXL scores and original ablation values are unchanged. v2 adds ImageRAG-F, GPTScore, additional-dataset, VLM-diagnostic and absolute-study results; the latter reports 92%, 90% and 84% concept presence for OmniGen, SDXL and FLUX on selected cases. FLUX baseline values also change, such as ImageNet CLIP from 0.262 to 0.271, but configuration equivalence is insufficiently documented to interpret this as a same-setting gain.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theoretical proofs or formal guarantees. The prompt template is restated for the already-used one-image-per-concept setting. The added chain-of-thought and retrieval explanations introduce no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains training-free, model-independent retrieval of references for missing concepts to improve rare and fine-grained generation. The third backbone and expanded evaluations support this existing claim. Calling the retained VLM stages guided chain-of-thought does not establish a different core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of why embedding metrics can miss fine-grained improvements and why CLIP retrieval can succeed when generation fails. It also discusses ambiguous prompts, hypothesizes why unrelated references are ignored, and characterizes model-dependent diversity versus faithfulness tradeoffs. Existing limitations concerning retrieval coverage, counting and text generation are retained and illustrated.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds FLUX-schnell/OminiControl settings, 50 inference steps, retrieval-threshold disclosure, and VLM timing and API-cost estimates. Section 8 promises code release, without establishing availability. Existing prompts and retry details are relocated, while v1's explicit 1024×1024 resolution and comparative-study decision-bypass disclosure are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 substantially updates positioning against close alternatives: RealRAG's trained retrieval module and FineRAG's retrieval of all concepts with layout construction. These comparisons sharpen the distinction of training-free, gap-directed retrieval beyond v1's contrast with RAG-trained generators. It also adds relevant chain-of-thought, editing, conditioning and evaluation references; RealRAG and FineRAG are discussed rather than directly benchmarked.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method and experimental narrative are extensively revised. Method exposition is reorganized around guided chain-of-thought; implementation, error handling, personalization and proprietary-data experiments move into appendices. Related-work subsections are consolidated, and reproducibility and LLM-usage statements are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with extensive figure and table restructuring. The teaser and qualitative comparison grids are revised, the user-study figure gains FLUX and absolute-evaluation panels, and new failure, ablation and diversity figures appear. Existing ablation and proprietary-result tables are split or regrouped, alongside new GPTScore and dataset tables.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's similarity metrics and relative preferences: the absolute human study checks concept presence on retrieval-triggered cases, while the controlled VLM experiment tests a central diagnostic assumption. Additional backbone coverage and explicit failure and diversity analyses strengthen applicability assessment. Unexplained FLUX reporting inconsistencies—the LAION-F rows in Tables 6–7 repeat base-FLUX values rather than Table 2's ImageRAG-F values—and some omitted protocol details limit parts of the evidence, but do not outweigh these gains.
